material.title_suggested: Things China's EVs Can Do That No American Car Can
material.advice: This material is dense with specific numbers and comparisons. Watch out for the long sentence in chunk 7 (list of actions) and the parallel structure in chunk 16. Practice chunk 7 by breaking it into three actions: attach, link, mirror. Use the numbers (360, 11 minutes, 350 kW, 1 MW) as anchors for chunks 2, 11, and 14. For chunk 16, emphasize the rhythm of the short sentences.

chunks.text: Three things China's EVs can do that no American car can. And Americans aren't allowed to buy any of them.
The BYD Yangwang U8 can spin a full 360° on solid concrete without moving forward or backward.
It can jump over potholes using active suspension that reads the road ahead.
And it floats on water. Not as a gimmick or a concept, but as a production feature on a car you can buy today.
Meanwhile, the Cybertruck, which cost more, got stuck in a car wash.
The Xiaomi SU7 lets you physically snap accessories onto the dashboard.
Magnetically attach a camera, link hardware buttons to whatever function you want on the screen, and it mirrors your phone without a subscription fee.
Yes, a subscription fee. Tesla would charge for everything, including features your car already has built in.
Xiaomi and others gives you a modular cockpit and charges you nothing extra.
Apple CarPlay? Tesla still doesn't offer it at any price.
And this one that changes everything. 10 to 80% in under 11 minutes.
This is not a lab result or a future promise. A production car you can buy in China or other parts of the world today.
By the time a Tesla owner finishes plugging into a supercharger, this car is already charged and moving.
America's fastest public chargers peak at 350 kW. And China deployed 1 MW charging this year.
None of these cars are available in America. Not because they failed a safety test, which they passed flawlessly.
It's not because Americans don't want them. These features exist. The technology is real. The price is lower.
Washington just decided you shouldn't have the choice.
